analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infrastructures is a tiny, cyclical civil construction contractor with no discernible moat, lumpy cash flows, and a revenue base that barely existed three years ago. At 26x P/E for a 13.6% ROE commodity-like contractor, there is no margin of safety and this sits well outside my circle of competence.
key_strengths: Debt reduced from INR 109 Cr (2022) to INR 60 Cr (2025); equity raised to INR 116 Cr strengthens balance sheet
Promoter holding at 72.38% shows skin in the game
ROCE of 15.5% and expanding EBITDA (INR 13→28 Cr) show operational improvement
key_risks: Civil construction is a low-moat, project-based, working-capital-heavy business with no pricing power
Revenue exploded from INR 1 Cr (2022) to INR 90 Cr (2025) — unproven durability; FY25 revenue actually dipped vs FY24
FCF collapsed from INR 11 Cr (2023) to INR 2 Cr (2025) despite higher profits — cash conversion is poor
red_flags: FY25 financing inflow of INR 63 Cr (likely IPO/fresh equity) inflating book value — recent listing with limited public track record
OCF crashed from INR 32 Cr (2024) to INR 5 Cr (2025) while net profit rose — working capital red flag typical of contractors
P/E of 26x on a ~INR 13 Cr profit base for a sub-INR 300 Cr micro-cap contractor is rich
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is precisely the kind of business I avoid: a small civil construction contractor whose financial history effectively begins in FY2023. The 348% revenue CAGR is mathematical noise from a near-zero base, and FY25 revenue (INR 90 Cr) actually declined from FY24 (INR 97 Cr), suggesting the growth narrative is already wobbling. Construction is a bid-based business with no brand power, no switching costs, no network effects, and no cost advantage at this scale — the definition of a fair business, not a wonderful one. ROE of 13.6% is below my 15% threshold, and with the recent equity raise diluting that base further, returns on the enlarged capital will likely compress.

The cash flow statement tells the real story: despite growing profits, FCF fell to just INR 2 Cr in FY25, and the INR 63 Cr financing inflow indicates this is a freshly capitalized entity still proving itself. Paying 26x earnings for a INR 267 Cr micro-cap contractor with lumpy cash conversion and no moat offers zero margin of safety. I'd pass without hesitation — there is nothing here a patient owner-investor should pay up for.
